channel.title: FXStreet Forex & Commodities News
channel.description: Real-time Forex News and the latest trading updates. Stay updated on the latest news about currencies and commodities markets.

item.title: Gold drops as Hormuz firefight fuels US Dollar jump
item.description: Gold (XAU/USD) price slumps over 1% on Wednesday, losing for the second day in the week amid fears that hostilities between the US and Iran may escalate, pushing energy prices higher and the US Dollar as well.

item.title: Canadian Dollar down despite soaring Oil Prices: What’s pressuring the CAD?
item.description: The Canadian Dollar (CAD) trades with a heavy tone against its American counterpart, as the US Dollar (USD) gathers strength from renewed Middle East concerns. The USD/CAD pair nears 1.3900, its highest in two months.

item.title: Japanese Yen: Markets eye 160 versus US Dollar on hawkish BoJ – Scotiabank
item.description: Scotiabank strategists Shaun Osborne and Eric Theoret note the Japanese Yen (JPY) is marginally stronger, with USD/JPY stabilizing just below the key 160 resistance area. They stress that intervention risk remains elevated as the pair approaches this psychologically important level.

item.title: Indonesian Rupiah: State-led commodity shift reshapes risks – MUFG
item.description: MUFG’s Lloyd Chan highlights that Indonesia is undergoing a structural regime shift as the state moves toward direct control of key commodity exports via Danantara Sumberdaya Indonesia.

item.title: 100.00: The United States Dollar Index retargets its psychological level
item.description: The US Dollar (USD) maintains its positive performance for the third consecutive day on Wednesday, this time lifting the US Dollar Index (DXY) to the vicinity of two-month highs near 99.50 and opening the door to a potential test of the psychological 100.00 hurdle in the relatively short term.

item.title: New Zealand Dollar weakens for third day as US-Iran tensions bolster Dollar
item.description: NZD/USD falls to around 0.5870 on Wednesday at the time of writing, down 0.97% on the day. The pair extends its bearish move for a third consecutive day as investors favor the US Dollar (USD) amid escalating geopolitical tensions in the Middle East.

item.title: Japanese Yen loses ground amid US PMI data
item.description: The USD/JPY pair is trading just below the 160.00 price level on Wednesday, as the US Dollar (USD) remains supported by stronger-than-expected economic data, while the Japanese Yen (JPY) struggles to attract sustained demand amid a cautious market mood.

item.title: India: Growth set to cool in early 2026 – DBS
item.description: DBS Group Research, led by Radhika Rao with contributions from Daisy Sharma, expects India’s real GDP growth to slow in early 2026 after a firm second half of FY26.

item.title: Euro slips against the US Dollar as upbeat US economic data reinforces hawkish Fed bets
item.description: EUR/USD ticks lower on Wednesday after closing the previous day virtually unchanged. The Euro (EUR) weakens as stronger-than-expected US economic data boosts demand for the US Dollar (USD), while renewed tensions in the Middle East further support the Greenback.

item.title: British Pound buckles as Hormuz attacks spark US Dollar rush
item.description: The Pound Sterling (GBP) drops by 0.28% during the North American session on Wednesday as the US and Iran exchange attacks, while data in the US showed that the labor market remains solid and that business activity expanded but is slowing.

item.title: British Pound: Range-bound versus US Dollar ahead of BoE – Scotiabank
item.description: Scotiabank strategists Shaun Osborne and Eric Theoret highlight that the British Pound (GBP) is trading fractionally lower against the Dollar, with limited fresh data beyond a slightly contractionary services PMI.

item.title: Japanese Yen: Intervention risk and BoJ shift – BBH
item.description: Brown Brothers Harriman’s (BBH) Elias Haddad reports that USD/JPY’s test of 160.00 has heightened intervention risks, with Japanese authorities already having spent a record amount to cap the pair near that level.

item.title: US Treasuries lost their crown: Why central banks are betting on Gold
item.description: Gold has become the top reserve asset in global central banks’ vaults, surpassing US Treasuries, suggesting that the precious metal is becoming the main choice for monetary authorities seeking protection against geopolitical uncertainty.

item.title: US Dollar Index: Tariff plans and conflict support Dollar – BNY
item.description: BNY’s Bob Savage reports that the Dollar Index is firmer as higher U.S. yields and renewed geopolitical tensions underpin safe-haven demand. President Trump’s proposal for broad new tariffs raises trade and inflation risks, reinforcing USD support.

item.title: Australian Dollar declines as disappointing GDP, firm US data bolster USD
item.description: AUD/USD trades around 0.7145 on Wednesday at the time of writing, down 0.50% on the day. The pair remains under pressure after the release of several disappointing Australian economic indicators, while solid US data continues to support the US Dollar (USD).

item.title: Canadian Dollar: Resistance caps losses against US Dollar – Scotiabank
item.description: Scotiabank strategists Shaun Osborne and Eric Theoret note the Canadian Dollar (CAD) remains soft but broadly stable, with USD/CAD trading near 1.3850.

item.title: Gold falls as strong US data and Middle East tensions boost the US Dollar
item.description: Gold (XAU/USD) trades lower on Wednesday as escalating tensions in the Middle East dampen hopes for a near-term US-Iran peace deal, while a fresh batch of upbeat US economic data reinforces expectations that interest rates could stay higher for longer.

item.title: Japanese Yen: Limited downside against US Dollar as BoJ signals hike – MUFG
item.description: MUFG’s Derek Halpenny notes that recent Ministry of Finance (MoF) and Bank of Japan (BoJ) intervention failed to prevent USD/JPY from returning to 160, as higher US yields and renewed Middle East tensions support the Dollar.

item.title: Fed's Williams: Policy in right place, no need to raise or lower rates
item.description: Federal Reserve (Fed) Bank of New York President John Williams said on Wednesday that higher energy prices are driving up costs and inflation, per Reuters.

item.title: Swiss Franc weakens against US Dollar after strong ADP and ISM Services PMI data
item.description: USD/CHF extends its advance on Wednesday as ongoing tensions in the Middle East and stronger-than-expected US labor data lift the US Dollar (USD). At the time of writing, the pair is trading around 0.7900, staying on the front foot for a third straight day.

item.title: Breaking: US ISM Services PMI rises to 54.5 in May vs. 53.8 expected
item.description: Business activity in the United States (US) service sector expanded at an accelerating pace in May, with the Institute for Supply Management's (ISM) Services Purchasing Managers' Index (PMI) rising to 54.5 from 53.6 in April. This reading came in better than the market expectation of 53.8.

item.title: Eurozone: Real yields and supply pressures – ING
item.description: ING’s Padhraic Garvey and Michiel Tukker stress that Eurozone real rates are increasingly driven by structural forces such as fiscal expansion and record bond supply. They point to rising 10Y euro implied real rates since 2024, helped by German spending plans.

item.title: United States S&P Global Services PMI misses estimates: US Dollar firms on risk aversion
item.description: The final reading of the United States (US) S&P Global Services PMI came in at 50.7 in May, down from 50.9 previously and missing estimates of 50.9. Meanwhile, the Composite PMI was confirmed at 51.5 in the same month, slightly below the anticipated 51.7.

item.title: Gold: CTA selling triggers and inflation headwinds – TD Securities
item.description: TD Securities’ Ryan McKay notes that Gold is struggling to recover as renewed tariffs and US-Iran tensions fuel an inflationary impulse and push expectations for a Federal Reserve (Fed) hike into early 2027.

item.title: India: RBI faces currency pressure – Societe Generale
item.description: Societe Generale’s Santosh Ejantkar and Tanmay Purohit note India’s equity market has slipped to seventh globally, overtaken by South Korea and Taiwan as their semiconductor-heavy markets benefit from the AI boom.

item.title: Australia: Growth momentum weakens as demand cools – UOB
item.description: UOB economist Lee Sue Ann highlights that Australia’s GDP growth slowed to 0.3% q/q in 1Q26 as weak public spending, trade drag and cyclone disruptions offset strong business investment.

item.title: GBP/JPY Price Forecast: Long-term moving averages continue to support the uptrend
item.description: GBP/JPY edges lower on Wednesday as fresh intervention warnings from Tokyo lift the Japanese Yen (JPY) across the board. At the time of writing, the cross trades around 214.82, down 0.25% on the day.

item.title: WTI Crude Oil surges on renewed Iran Gulf tensions, sharp US inventory drawdown
item.description: West Texas Intermediate (WTI) advances toward $94.00 at the time of writing, up 2.52% on the day, supported by a fresh escalation of geopolitical tensions in the Middle East and growing concerns about global Oil supplies.

item.title: Japanese Yen: Intervention risk shapes FX focus – BNY
item.description: BNY’s Bob Savage highlights that USD/JPY remains close to 160.00 as markets price a high probability of a June BoJ rate hike, yet see Governor Ueda as insufficiently hawkish. Japanese authorities stress G7 agreement on limiting excessive FX volatility and pledge cooperation with the U.S.

item.title: Bank of England: July risk as energy flows stay fragile – ING
item.description: ING economist James Smith argues that a June Bank of England (BoE) rate hike now appears unlikely as weaker United Kingdom (UK) data and lower Oil prices ease pressure on policymakers.
